verdict: The single biggest lie this UI tells: it claims to be a building but it is one reusable component. Every screen — floor, locker room, office, profile — is the same centered, rounded, dark panel floating in a vignette void, wearing different data. That is a dark-mode SaaS with a sepia filter, exactly the failure the brief names. Light comes from nowhere: shadows are elevation tokens, glows are emissive pixels, hover states levitate cards. The palette is genuinely good and the writing already lives in 1975, which makes the chrome's betrayal louder — pill chips, badge counters, segmented controls, native selects, breadcrumbs. Nothing on screen answers "what object is this?" There is no wall, no desk, no gravity. The set is built from Figma parts painted brown.

proposals.detail: Kill the floating-panel shell (radius-lg + vignette + backdrop-filter). Every screen gets a full-bleed environment: painted cinder block, aged plaster, or steel via 2-3 layered gradients plus one shared SVG feTurbulence noise filter (defined once, referenced everywhere at low opacity). Content mounts ON that wall — corkboard, clipboard hung on a nail, filing cabinet drawer — and touches the viewport edges. Shadows become contact shadows cast by a consistent light direction, not elevation halos.

Rebuild the floor nav as a scene of five DIFFERENT objects: the office is a frosted-glass door with hand-painted arc lettering (SVG textPath, gold paint with chipped edge masks); the locker room a battleship-grey steel door with stenciled letters; the press a stack of newspapers on a bench; the calendar a tear-off wall pad by the light switch. Different widths, heights, baselines; each rotated ±0.3-0.8deg. Hover = the room's light comes on (brightness/glow inside the door glass), never translateY lift.

proposals.idea: The fighter is a manila folder
proposals.detail: FighterProfile becomes an open file folder on a desk blotter: kraft-paper texture (gradient + noise), tabs become physical folder tabs cut into the top edge (clip-path trapezoids at staggered heights, the active one pulled forward, one dog-eared), photo attached with a real staple (tiny SVG) and photo-corner shadows, vitals typed on an index card in Special Elite with uneven ink density (subtle per-character opacity via text-shadow tricks or an SVG displacement filter).

Attributes become a typed evaluation sheet: typewriter numerals as the primary read, and instead of glowing bars a hand-drawn pencil gauge — an SVG line with feTurbulence displacement so it wobbles, graphite grey, length still proportional so scannability survives. Trend arrows become pencil ticks; 'FOCUSED · FOOTWORK' becomes a red grease-pencil circle around the FOOTWORK row (SVG ellipse, rough stroke).

proposals.idea: Stamps and slips replace pills and badges
proposals.detail: One reusable .stamp primitive: uppercase condensed type inside a rough border, rotated 1-3deg, red or blue ink, mask-image noise for uneven inking — replaces MoodChip, TraitChip, DEVELOPING/ESTABLISHED tags, and MUST KEEP/WATCH LIST/CHOPPING BLOCK (which becomes a stamp choice on the folder cover). The notification badge dies: waiting walk-ins are pink 'WHILE YOU WERE OUT' slips fanned under the office door, count = number of visible slips.

proposals.idea: One light rig for the whole building
proposals.detail: A global lighting layer per room, composed of: a warm desk-lamp pool (radial gradient anchored to an actual lamp object), a cool dusty window shaft (angled linear gradient + noise, low opacity), and for the locker room a green-white fluorescent tone with a 0.2s flicker keyframe at long random intervals. All object shadows share one direction per room. Interactivity = light catching brass or paper lifting a few px with a hinged rotateX, never glow tokens.

Reassign the existing fonts to physical origins and add two: a period cursive/marker for trainer handwriting and a stencil for painted signage. Big Shoulders = painted posters/signage only; Special Elite = anything the gym typed (rosters, profiles, ledgers); Roboto Slab = newsprint only, inside newspaper objects only; Oswald microtype breadcrumbs are banned. Rule: if you cannot name the object that produced the text (typewriter, sign painter, newspaper press, rubber stamp, pencil), it does not ship.

proposals.idea: Time is a punch clock and a tear-off calendar
proposals.detail: Replace ADVANCE DAY / ADVANCE WEEK buttons with a wall-mounted punch clock (steel case, bakelite lever — CSS 3D press with a satisfying 2-frame travel) for +1 day, and tearing the top page off the wall calendar pad for +1 week (page rotates and falls via CSS transform, next date revealed beneath). The date itself IS the calendar pad; the SPRING · 1975 CAREER strip becomes a printed line on the pad's header. Zero information lost, one HUD strip removed.

hills: No floating panels, no voids: every screen must have a wall, a floor, and gravity. If an element casts a shadow, a named light source in the room casts it. The room-shell component (centered rounded panel over vignette) is deleted, not restyled.

Every interactive control must pass the object test — 'what physical thing is this?' — before it ships. Pills, badges, segmented controls, native selects, and glow effects are banned outright, with a required period replacement (stamp, slip, folder tab, toggle, lever) specified at design time, never 'later'.

Information density and decision speed are preserved to the number: the typed sheet must scan as fast as the bar chart it replaces (proportional pencil gauges stay), and no physical transition exceeds ~300ms. Atmosphere that taxes the player's time gets cut before it gets shipped.
fights: Accessibility will object to graphite-pencil gauges, stamped labels, and low-contrast handwritten marginalia replacing high-contrast bars and pills. I will concede ink density and font size, never the object language — a darker pencil, not a glowing bar.

Engineering will object to five bespoke door objects, per-room light rigs, and SVG noise/displacement filters versus the current single reusable panel + token system, on cost and maintenance grounds. My position: the reusable-panel abstraction IS the bug; I will accept a shared texture/stamp/paper primitive library, not a shared room shell.

UX/Systems design will object that folders, punch clocks, and tear-off calendars add clicks and animation time versus tabs and buttons, hurting the fast-decision loop the owner demands. I will cap every physical transition and keep hit targets identical, but I will not restore modern chrome as a 'power user mode' — there is one world, and it is 1975.

verdict: This is a competently built modern dashboard in sepia: hierarchy, density, and decision paths are genuinely sound, and near-zero physicality. That's good news — the interaction skeleton (roster scan, one-screen fighter decisions, two-button time advance) can survive a full surface transplant untouched. Everything visible reads 2025: hover-lifted cards in a perfect 5-column grid, pill chips, glowing rounded progress bars, native selects, an iOS notification badge, centered web modals. But the fix is not to blur, rotate, and darken — it's to swap the component vocabulary (stamped forms, typed rosters, pinned notes, checklists) while keeping alignment, contrast, and click-costs identical or better. Paper is a human-factors gift: dark ink on parchment out-contrasts amber-on-leather everywhere. The rule that reconciles both masters: jitter the decoration, never the data.

proposals.idea: Jitter decoration, never data (the governing rule)
proposals.detail: Codify a two-layer standard in theme.css: a DECOR layer (paper edges, tape, stains, rotation up to 2deg, SVG feTurbulence grain) and a DATA layer (names, numbers, bars, buttons' labels) that stays orthogonal, aligned, and unfiltered. Rotation applies to the paper object via transform on the container; an inner counter-rotated or unrotated text block holds compared numerals. This single constraint lets the art team go feral on materials without costing one millisecond of scan time.

proposals.idea: Attribute bars become a printed evaluation form with grease-pencil fill
proposals.detail: Replace AttributeBar with a parchment 'FIGHTER EVALUATION' form: printed ruled scale (tick marks every 10, printed via repeating-linear-gradient), attribute names in a government-form face (e.g. a condensed grotesque, all caps, printed ink #2a2118), fill drawn as a flat-ended grease-pencil stroke (SVG path with feTurbulence displacement, no border-radius, no glow), number typed in a fixed right column with tabular figures. Length-encoding is preserved exactly — same pre-attentive read, higher contrast than amber-on-leather, zero modern tells.

proposals.idea: Chips become rubber stamps with a fixed color+angle code
proposals.detail: TraitChip/MoodChip/trajectory pills become rubber-stamp impressions: uppercase slab/stencil face, uneven ink via SVG filter, each CATEGORY gets one fixed ink color and one fixed angle (e.g. trajectory = red at -2deg, mood = blue-black at 0deg, scouting feel = green at +1.5deg). Consistency is what makes stamps pre-attentively scannable down a roster column; random angles per instance would destroy that. MUST KEEP / WATCH / CHOPPING BLOCK becomes a colored card-stock tag clipped to the folder edge — three fixed positions, one click, same semantics.

proposals.idea: Native selects become printed checklists with pencil checkmarks
proposals.detail: Training focus: a printed list of all focuses on the form, one pencil checkmark (hand-drawn SVG check) marking the active one; click a line to move the check. Trainer assignment: a small pegboard of trainer name-tags with hooks. This is strictly better ergonomics than a <select> — all options visible (no hidden state, no extra click to open), larger targets, and it reads as paperwork. Keep keyboard support: the list is a styled radiogroup.

proposals.idea: Notices become paper that arrives on a desk blotter
proposals.detail: Replace the centered modal with a diegetic document: telegram/memo slip that slides onto a desk-blotter layer at the bottom-center with a settle animation (<300ms), one visible fold, paperclip if multi-page. Actions become stamps inked onto the paper ('SEEN', 'LATER') — big rectangular targets, ≥44px. Keep focus trap, Esc-to-dismiss, and the same two-action structure. Badge counts become a visible stack of slips (2 slips = 2 notices) plus a stamped numeral for exact count.

proposals.idea: The floor nav becomes five DIFFERENT objects
proposals.detail: Office = wooden door with frosted-glass pane and painted gold lettering; Locker Room = open doorway with steel-locker gleam beyond; My Gym = painted wall sign over the ring apron; Press = newspaper rack/stack; Calendar = wall calendar under a bare bulb. Differentiated silhouettes are a recognition upgrade over five identical cards (shape recognition beats label reading). Non-negotiables: same left-to-right order forever, hit areas no smaller than current cards, a lit hover state that brightens the object's own lamp rather than lifting it.

proposals.idea: Development table becomes a typewritten roster sheet — alignment sacred
proposals.detail: The devview table renders as a typed page (Special Elite or similar) on a clipboard: typewriter is genuinely monospaced, so columns self-align better than the current mixed-face table. Trend arrows become pencil ticks (↑ as a small hand-drawn caret in graphite, ↓ in red pencil) in their own column. Row hover = a fingertip smudge highlight, not a background fill. Column headers rubber-stamped once at top. Density stays identical; scanning improves because every numeral occupies the same advance width.

proposals.idea: Environmental lighting with a contrast floor
proposals.detail: Desk-lamp pools, dusty window shafts, and fluorescent flicker live in a background layer (radial-gradients + one shared SVG grain), but define a 'reading layer' rule: any surface holding decision text is parchment or chalkboard and measures ≥4.5:1 (target 7:1 for numerals) AFTER the lighting layer composites. Vignette may only touch the outer 10% of content panels. This makes the lighting the room's, not the screen's, without ever making a tired player lean in — these sessions run hundreds of Advance Weeks.

hills: Jitter decoration, never data: compared numerals and names sit in strictly aligned columns with tabular figures; any text block used for a decision rotates at most 2 degrees, and numeric columns rotate 0. If a stain or tape ever overlaps a numeral, the design ships broken.

Contrast floor is diegetic-proof: every piece of decision-critical text meets 4.5:1 (numerals 7:1) under the final composited lighting. Handwriting and pencil are flavor channels only — never the sole carrier of a stat, price, or deadline.

Interaction cost never increases: every physical replacement costs the same clicks or fewer than the widget it replaces, targets stay ≥44px, and the two most frequent actions (Advance Day/Week, assign training) remain one visible click from their screens. No drawer-opening, no drag-to-file, no 'realistic' friction on frequent paths.
fights: Art direction: they will push heavier vignettes, deeper shadow, and per-instance random rotation/stains on paper because it photographs beautifully. I will block any lighting that drops reading surfaces below the contrast floor and any randomness that touches data columns — the mockup that wins the pitch is the screen that exhausts the player by week 40.

Narrative/worldbuilding: they will want handwritten trainer scrawl as the primary voice for fighter evaluations and scouting reads ('the trainer's notebook IS the truth'). Handwriting at roster-scan sizes is illegible and unscannable across 8 lockers; I insist typewriter/stamp carries anything read repeatedly, with handwriting reserved for one-line marginalia the player reads once.

Engineering/performance: they will object to SVG feTurbulence filters and layered gradients on every surface (paint cost, low-end GPUs). I'll concede shared filter defs and pre-baked noise as data-URI tiles, but I will not accept 'flat color with a border' as the fallback — a flat fallback silently reintroduces the exact modern look this overhaul exists to kill.

role: Information Architect — navigation as wayfinding in a building
verdict: The building doesn't exist. There is a floor screen and four "rooms," but every room is the same object: a rounded panel floating over a dimming scrim, reached from a row of five identical feature-cards with marketing taglines, navigated by breadcrumbs, segmented tab controls, and red notification badges. Two of the five rooms (The Press, Calendar) aren't rooms at all — they're objects that got promoted to routes because the router needed entries. Nothing has a physical address: finances, rivals, and walk-ins all live "in a centered panel behind a tab," so the player builds no spatial memory and the environment communicates nothing with labels removed. The functional skeleton is genuinely good — shallow depth, one overlay layer, Esc backs out — which means the IA can keep its bones while every wall gets rebuilt.

proposals.detail: Replace the five cards with one asymmetric SVG set viewed from the floor: the office door (frosted glass, hand-painted "OFFICE" lettering) at one side; a doorway into the locker corridor (glimpse of steel lockers and a hanging bulb); the ring and bags as ambient center; a wall calendar hanging crooked; the day's newspaper folded on a bench. Calendar becomes the wall calendar object (floor and office). Clicking an object zooms to it full-frame. The building becomes architecturally honest: Floor, Office, Locker Room — everything else is furniture, which is exactly what a struggling gym has.

proposals.idea: The office is one desk you look down at
proposals.detail: Kill the office tab bar. Render a continuous desk scene: blotter center with the walk-in cards stacked in a wire inbox tray; a cloth-bound ledger at the right (opening it IS Finances — ruled paper, hand-entered figures); a two-drawer filing cabinet at the frame edge labeled with taped index cards ("RIVALS", "LEDGER/HISTORY"); the folded newspaper at the corner. Every category gets a permanent physical address; the player reaches for the ledger the way they reach for a real one. CSS: one background SVG, absolutely-positioned object hotspots, per-object zoom transitions.

FighterProfile becomes a folder pulled from the cabinet: die-cut folder tabs along the top edge at staggered offsets (OVERVIEW/RECORD/BIO/CAREER/DEVELOPMENT as typewriter labels on the tabs — an SVG path per tab, not equal-width buttons), photo paper-clipped top-left, attributes as a typed carbon sheet with rubber-stamped figures, scouting reads in a handwritten hand, and the MUST KEEP/WATCH/CHOPPING BLOCK control replaced by a grease-pencil circle or colored tab clipped to the folder edge. Same data density, different object.

proposals.idea: Counts are visible evidence, not badges
proposals.detail: Delete every numeric badge. Walk-ins waiting = card silhouettes visible in the inbox tray / shapes behind the office door's frosted glass; roster size = which lockers hang open; new mail = envelope sticking out of the door slot; coach applicants = notices pinned to the corkboard. Keep exact counts in title/aria-label so nothing is lost to assistive tech or hover.

Remove .room-screen__breadcrumb and the chrome back button. Where you ARE is the room's own signage (painted glass, a brass plaque, stenciled letters on the locker-corridor wall). The way BACK is a sliver of the previous space at the screen edge — the open door with the floor visible through it — clickable, with Esc preserved. Wayfinding by looking, not by reading a path string.

Advance Day = tearing a page off a desk date pad (CSS transform tear animation on an SVG pad showing FRI / MAY 2); Advance Week = flipping the wall calendar's page. The footer bar dies; the current date is the calendar and pad themselves, readable at a glance from the floor. Season/era context comes from the calendar's printed month artwork.

Remove the room panel's border-radius, max-width, and scrim. Entering a room is a camera cut/pan: the set fills the viewport edge-to-edge with its own environmental light source (desk lamp pool in the office, fluorescent tube glare in the locker corridor). The existing overlay architecture (RoomRouter stacking) can stay under the hood — only the visual treatment changes from lightbox to film cut, via full-bleed layout and a short transform transition.

hills: Location equals meaning: every category of information gets exactly one permanent physical address the player could point to with the labels stripped — finances are the ledger ON the desk, rivals are IN the filing cabinet, the roster IS the locker wall. No information may live in an abstract floating panel.
Nothing gets to be a 'room' unless a 1975 gym would have that room. The Press and the Calendar are objects, not architecture — a route table entry is not a reason to build a fake wall.

Zero abstract navigation chrome: no breadcrumbs, no notification badges, no segmented controls in a header bar. Wayfinding happens by looking at the set (signage, open doors, visible evidence), with counts and paths preserved invisibly in aria labels.

My position: primary values (numbers, names, actions) stay fully legible; annotation flavor is ALLOWED to be dim, because a real trainer's pencil note is dim. Every container must pass the object test: if you cannot name the physical thing it is (folder, index card, clipboard, plaque, memo slip, ledger page), it does not ship. 'Panel' is not an object.

Imperfection must be deterministic and small: seeded per entity ID, max ~2deg rotation and ~6px drift, identical every render. Random-per-mount jitter reads as a glitch, and large chaos costs usability — both are worse than perfect grids.

The graphic voice is one voice: tracked-out Oswald micro-caps label every information type, so a newspaper date, a locker count, and a stat name all speak like a 2024 design system. role: Art Director / Production Designer — the cinematic whole: one film, one look, one camera
verdict: This is a modern dark-mode product wearing a sepia color grade — exactly what the owner said he doesn't want. There is no camera. Declare a light source per room and enforce it with a fixed full-viewport overlay layer: office = tungsten desk lamp, radial warm pool upper-left, everything falls off to umber; locker room = one buzzing fluorescent tube, slightly green-cyan cast (a subtle hue-rotate on that room only), hard top-down falloff; press = grey daylight through a dusty window, cool and flat. verdict: This is a dark-mode SaaS product art-directed in sepia. Exactly two real props exist — the walk-in card and the newspaper — and even those float, centered and rounded, over a void. Everything else is naked software: a five-card dashboard grid pretending to be a gym floor, segmented-control tabs, glowing pill progress bars, label chips, native OS selects, notification badges with pulse animations, and a persistent app header with breadcrumbs. The lighting is a vignette gradient, not a lamp; the "room" has no walls, no floor material, no furniture, nothing to rest anything on. The palette is right and the writing is superb — the set is simply missing. Nothing here would survive the "remove the labels" test; you'd see a generic dark admin panel.

The header bar itself is demolished — the gym name becomes the painted window sign, mirrored, seen from inside.

Mood/status = rubber stamps: double-ring or boxed border SVG, stamp-pad red or blue-black ink, uneven coverage via mask-image noise, each stamped at a seeded -3..3deg rotation ('CONTENT', 'PLATEAUED', 'MUST KEEP' begs to be a stamp). Traits = strips of masking tape (torn ends via clip-path polygon, slight shadow, marker lettering). Trajectory tags on the development clipboard = colored grease-pencil underlines rather than pills. One shared .stamp/.tape utility class each, so the treatment is systemic.

Extend theme.css with material tokens: --paper-grain, --steel, --concrete, --chalk, plus a single inline-SVG feTurbulence data-URI reused as grain overlay per material class. Every named light source gets a CSS layer: office desk lamp (warm 2700K radial, hard elliptical falloff on the desk), locker room fluorescent (slightly green top-down strip light, subtle 8s flicker on one tube), floor bulbs (visible cords, pools). All paper gets seeded 0.3–1.5deg rotation, a dog-ear or tape corner; all metal gets rust blooms at screw positions (radial-gradient spots). Ban backdrop-filter and box-shadow glows repo-wide.

hills: Every surface must rest on something. No element may float over void with a drop shadow — if I cannot answer 'what is this pinned to, lying on, or bolted to?' (wall, desk, clipboard, folder, corkboard, door), it does not ship. The current .fp__card, room-door grid, and every modal all fail this test.

Every typeface needs a diegetic source. Type is only allowed if I can name the machine or hand that made it: letterpress poster, typewriter, rubber stamp, stencil, ballpoint, grease pencil, newsprint. Generic condensed-caps-with-0.2em-tracking UI labeling (the current chrome, chips, and section headers) is forbidden on props.

Nothing glows and nothing blurs. Light comes from fixtures — lamps, tubes, windows — and falls ON objects; objects never emit. Every box-shadow glow (amber button halos, attr-bar glow, badge pulse) and every backdrop-filter is cut, replaced by placement inside a light pool.
fights: UX/Accessibility will fight my pencil-tick attribute scales, chalk text, and stamped statuses as lower-contrast and slower to scan than glowing bars and pill chips. I will keep the typewriter numeral column for instant reads, but the luminous bar dies — I won't restore glow to buy contrast; I'll buy it with paper value and ink weight.

Engineering will resist replacing native <select> with custom paper popovers (focus management, mobile behavior) and will flag per-element seeded rotations and feTurbulence filters as render cost and code sprawl. I hold: two OS dropdowns on the hero screen are a fiction-breaking bug, not a nice-to-have, and one shared grain asset + CSS custom properties keeps the cost bounded.

Game/systems design will defend the red count badge and the interrupting VIEW NOW modal as necessary for event visibility and pacing. I say envelopes jammed in a mail slot and a note under the door communicate 'two things happened, one is urgent' diegetically — if players genuinely miss events, we add a ringing desk phone, not a pulsing red circle.

role: Environmental Storytelling Specialist + Museum Exhibit Designer
verdict: The simulation remembers everything; the building remembers nothing. The data bones are superb — save.history, gym-log milestones, trait reveals, founding years, press clippings with bylines — but every trace of memory renders as a scrolling widget: ledger rows with border-bottoms, a dot timeline, KPI stat tiles, a collapsible drawer that only a code comment calls a corkboard. The environment itself is amnesiac: the floor is five identical nav cards floating in a void, lockers are factory clones that show no trace of past occupants, and the .worn grain-vignette fakes age the museum-replica way — uniformly, causelessly. A 20-year save and a day-one save are pixel-identical except the numbers. The game already generates a history worth exhibiting; the UI files it in a feed instead of hanging it on the wall.

offenders.where: GymScreen.tsx/.css — the gym floor (floor5.png): .gym__rooms is grid-template-columns: repeat(5, 1fr) of identical dark cards with thin line icons
offenders.tell: A dashboard home screen of nav cards hovering in empty space, perfectly symmetrical, identical materials
offenders.why: This is the room the player lives in for 20 years and it can never accumulate anything — no wall, no floor, no objects, so no place for history to physically land. A gym floor that looks the same on day 7,300 as day 1 kills the entire fantasy.

offenders.where: FighterProfile Record tab (tab_record.png): 3x3 grid of stat tiles — 'PROFESSIONAL 0-0-0', 'KO WINS 0', 'CAREER EARNINGS $0'
offenders.tell: KPI dashboard tiles with eyebrow labels, straight out of an analytics product
offenders.why: A fighter's record in 1975 is a typed card in a commission file or a line in Ring Record Book — a document with provenance. Tiles have no source, no author, no age; they're data with nowhere to have come from.

offenders.where: FighterProfile Career tab (tab_career.png): vertical timeline with connector line and dots, plus italic empty-state promise text
offenders.tell: The LinkedIn/Notion activity-timeline widget
offenders.why: A career is the single richest memory object in the game and it's rendered as the most recognizably modern component in the app. Nobody in 1975 drew dot timelines; they kept fight-by-fight record sheets that got longer, stapled, and annotated.

offenders.where: GymLogBoard.tsx (floor5.png bottom-left): rounded dark panel, '—' collapse toggle, '+3' unread counter
offenders.tell: A notification drawer / activity feed with unread badge
offenders.why: The code comment says 'the corkboard on the gym floor' but nothing rendered is cork, pinned, or paper. The gym's daily memory — the most atmospheric writing in the game — arrives as toast-adjacent chrome instead of notes physically pinned where they'd stay.

offenders.where: OfficeRoom.tsx LedgerTab / OfficeRoom.css .ledgerbook: flex column of rows with 1px border-bottoms inside a rounded, box-shadowed panel
offenders.tell: A data table in a floating card; 'entries' counter in the header like a query result count
offenders.why: 'What happened here, written down. Gyms forget nothing' — and then it renders as an infinite scroll feed. A ledger is a bound book: ruled pages, ink, handwriting that changes over years. The one object whose whole job is memory has no material memory.

offenders.where: GymScreen room doors (frontpage.png, poach_notice.png): red circular numeric badge '2' on the My Office card
offenders.tell: An iOS app-icon notification badge
offenders.why: It is the single most anachronistic pixel in the game. In a physical office, pending business is paper visibly waiting on the desk — envelopes under the door, a stack you can see — not a floating red dot.

offenders.where: LockerWall.css / wall8.png: identical locker clones, hover translateY(-3px) + amber glow ring, letterspaced 'EMPTY' microtype
offenders.tell: Interactive component states (lift-on-hover, focus glow) applied to what should be 300 lbs of bolted steel
offenders.why: Steel lockers don't levitate. Worse for my seat: lockers never remember occupants — a locker a champion used for five years looks identical to one never opened. Empty lockers are factory-new forever; the wall can't age.

offenders.where: Locker Room header + Development view (wall8.png, devview2.png): thin rounded progress bar for '3/8 LOCKERS', WALL/LIST/DEVELOPMENT segmented toggle, pill trait chips ('A NATURAL', 'PLATEAUED')
offenders.tell: Progress bars, segmented controls, and status pills — the core vocabulary of 2025 SaaS
offenders.why: Capacity in a real locker room is self-evident: you count the doors with names. The pill chips especially read as software tags; a trainer's read on a fighter belongs in pencil on a clipboard, not in a rounded outline chip.

proposals.detail: Derive a --gym-age custom property (0–1) from save.dayCount and drive LOCAL, caused wear with it: radial-gradient hand-smudge darkening around door handles and the calendar, scuff streaks at thresholds, paint loss at corners via layered SVG turbulence masks whose opacity scales with age. Wear concentrates where the player clicks most — the interface literally polishes and grimes where hands go. All CSS/SVG today; each wear patch is a registry slot real art can replace.

Give the gym floor an actual wall plane (perspective-tilted CSS surface over the existing backdrop). Every save.history milestone of sufficient weight spawns a physical exhibit: framed press clipping (generated from the existing press engine, sepia filter keyed to its age), a cheap bowling-trophy-grade SVG trophy on a plank shelf, a painted plywood board of house records hand-lettered per champion. Deterministic per-item rotation jitter (±2°, seeded by entry id) so frames hang crooked but stably. Twenty years in, the wall is full — that IS the save file, visible.

Rebuild LedgerTab as a two-page spread: ruled lines via repeating-linear-gradient, red margin rule, entries in a handwriting-adjacent font (Caveat/Homemade Apple class, with Special Elite for official items), pages turned by year instead of infinite scroll. Ink ages: color interpolates from near-black to faded brown by (today − entry.dayCount). Coffee-ring SVG and pencil marginalia seeded per page. Older years literally look older — the book exhibits time instead of listing it.

proposals.idea: Career = record card in a manila folder
proposals.detail: Replace the dot timeline with a commission-style fight record card: typed rows (typewriter font) on yellowed card stock, a rubber-stamped 'PRO DEBUT' / 'TITLE BOUT' (SVG stamp with uneven ink via feTurbulence displacement), paperclip and staple SVGs, and life events added in pen — the TYPE SOURCE encodes when and by whom a fact was recorded. Empty state: a fresh blank card with only the name typed, which is itself evocative.

Persist per-slot occupant history in the save. A vacated locker keeps a tape-residue ghost where the name was; a fighter cut on bad terms leaves a dent (SVG dark crease); a champion's old locker gets a small painted star and nobody uses it. Empty lockers vary by seeded slot: one repainted a slightly-off green, one door ajar, rust blooms at hinge screws scaling with slot age. Replace hover-lift with a door-crack: 1–2° rotateY hinge and interior shadow. The wall becomes a strata dig of everyone who ever trained here.

Replace ADVANCE DAY/WEEK buttons with physical time objects: a tear-off wall calendar (Advance Day rips a page — quick CSS transform + falling page; remaining-page thickness visible as stacked edges) and a wall clock or punch-clock for the week. The Gym Log becomes real cork: SVG cork texture, index cards and torn notebook paper overlapping at seeded angles, pushpins with cast shadows; old notes don't vanish — they slide under new ones and sun-fade, so the board itself has stratigraphy.

Add a 'clip this' scissors affordance to press stories about your gym. Clippings get pinned to the office corkboard / pasted in a scrapbook page; yellowing (sepia + brightness filter) driven by clip age. This turns the excellent-but-ephemeral press system into the player's self-curated museum — by year 20 the office wall is a biography the player chose. Cap the visible layer, archive the rest in the scrapbook to keep DOM sane.

Every purchased upgrade or damaging event leaves a permanent, dated repair: a plywood patch over a window, a rectangle of mismatched paint where a leak was fixed, new ring rope conspicuously whiter than the old. Each is an SVG overlay slot in the asset registry with a hover caption in the trainer's voice ('Pipe burst, winter of \'78. Sal fixed it for beer'). Repairs are the honest way a poor gym shows history — it never renovates, it patches.

hills: A 20-year save must be visually distinguishable from a day-one save at a glance with every label removed. If the environment doesn't accumulate — wear, trophies, clippings, tape ghosts — the 'building has memories' brief has failed, whatever the widgets look like.

No uniform aging shader. The current .worn grain+vignette ages everything equally, which is exactly how museum replicas ring false. Real wear is local, caused, and dated: dark where hands touch, stained where the mug sits, faded where the sun hits. Age must have provenance or it's set dressing.

Nothing that records the past may render as a feed, timeline, or stat tile. Memory lives in objects — a book, a clipping, a stamp, residue on steel — never in a scrolling list with border-bottoms. The ledger, the career tab, and the gym log are the soul of this game and they get object treatment first.
fights: Engineering/performance will object that persistent per-slot locker history, seeded wear overlays, and 20 years of accumulated clippings bloat the save schema and the DOM. I'll concede virtualization and layer caps, but not deletion: artifacts must persist across the whole save, because pruning history is exactly the amnesia I'm here to prevent.

Accessibility/readability will fight my faded ink, handwriting fonts, sepia clippings, and crooked pinned notes as contrast and legibility violations. I'll accept a 'lean in to read' focused state that flattens and brightens any document on inspection — but the at-rest state stays aged; I will not ship uniformly high-contrast paper that looks printed yesterday.

Design-system/token discipline will resist my core doctrine that nothing matches — the off-green repainted locker, mismatched paint patches, per-item rotation jitter break palette and component consistency by design. Their consistency instinct is correct for software and fatal for a place assembled over 20 years; variance must be seeded and intentional, but it must exist.

verdict: The four-font system is one modern voice wearing four costumes. The app's true typeface is not any of the four — it is "Oswald, uppercase, +0.1 to +0.3em tracking," used 119 times for section overlines, tabs, buttons, chips, column headers, and datelines; that habit alone is the Linear/Stripe signature and accounts for most of the modern feel. Big Shoulders Display (2019 Chicago-branding face) reads as sports-app branding, not wood type; Roboto Slab is Android-era and, fatally, doubles as newsprint body. Special Elite is the only genuine 1975 source in the stack and it is underused. Nothing is mixed by SOURCE — newspaper, magazine, form, plaque, and HUD are all set by the same 2025 designer with one spacing system. Missing entirely: blackletter/news serif, government-form print, handwriting, rubber stamps, fat-face poster wood type.

offenders.where: Everywhere — src/styles/theme.css --font-condensed + 151 letter-spacing / 110 uppercase declarations across src/**/*.css (e.g. FighterProfile.css section heads 'ATTRIBUTES', 'WHAT YOU KNOW', 'STANDING & TRAINING')
offenders.tell: Tracked-out uppercase Oswald overline microlabels (+0.1em to +0.3em) as the universal labeling system
offenders.why: This exact pattern is the house style of Linear, Stripe, and Notion. No 1975 object — form, sign, stamp, or typescript — letterspaces lowercase-sized labels this way; it instantly reads as a design-token system, not a place.

offenders.where: index.html font link + theme.css:47 --font-display: 'Big Shoulders Display' (headers like 'Locker Room', 'The New York Register', room card titles)
offenders.tell: A 2019 digital-branding condensed grotesque used as the period display face
offenders.why: Big Shoulders was designed for Chicago civic branding; its squarish modern skeleton reads DAZN/ESPN-app, not wood-type fight poster. The game's loudest type is its most anachronistic.

offenders.where: src/rooms/PressRoom.css — The Paper (press_paper.png): masthead, amber 'APR 27 '75' date labels, 'SPORTING PAGES · FRIDAY, MAY 2, 1975' dateline
offenders.tell: Newspaper set in the app's own design system: slab masthead, amber tracked-caps sans datelines, no headlines, ragged-right columns
offenders.why: A 1975 sports page means blackletter or Caslon masthead, bold condensed gothic headlines per story, justified hyphenated Linotype body, agate datelines in black ink. Amber-colored UI labels printed on newsprint is a physically impossible object — this screen should be the game's strongest period anchor and it's its weakest.

offenders.where: src/rooms/PressRoom.css — The Magazine (audit_magazine.png)
offenders.tell: The 'magazine' is a dark-background data table in the same Oswald/slab HUD voice
offenders.why: Magazines are paper. Ring Magazine 1975 means cream stock, Cooper-Black-era display, Century-style body, agate ratings tables. As rendered it is an analytics dashboard with a masthead.

offenders.where: src/screens/FighterProfile.css tab row (OVERVIEW / RECORD / BIOGRAPHY / CAREER / DEVELOPMENT)
offenders.tell: Equal-width bordered uppercase segmented-control tabs, identical type across states
offenders.why: This is a browser tab bar. The brief's own answer is folder tabs: die-cut manila dividers with typed or hand-inked labels, staggered heights, the active folder pulled forward — type should change source, not just background color.

offenders.where: src/components/MoodChip, TraitChip, LockerRoom dev table (devview2.png: 'DEVELOPING', 'A NATURAL', 'SLOW STUDY'; tab_overview.png: 'COMING ON', 'CONTENT')
offenders.tell: Rounded-outline status pills in tracked caps, semantically color-coded green/amber
offenders.why: These are GitHub labels / Notion tags — the purest 2020s component in the game. 1975 status marks are rubber stamps, grease-pencil circles, and typed margin notes, not vector pills.

offenders.where: src/components/TimeControls.css + dialog CTAs (floor5.png 'ADVANCE DAY +1', poach_notice.png 'VIEW NOW', frontpage.png 'REVIEW AT THE DOOR')
offenders.tell: Bordered-rectangle buttons with tracked uppercase Oswald and a superscript '+1' modifier
offenders.why: No physical source: not a plaque, not a stamped sign, not a painted switch label. The '+1/+7' notation is pure software affordance; a wall calendar or a punch clock would carry this action in the fiction.

offenders.where: src/components/WalkInCard/WalkInCard.css field labels (walkin_read2.png 'NAME:', 'AGE:', 'WEIGHT CLASS:' vs right-aligned bold slab values)
offenders.tell: Web-form label/value pairs: tracked caps labels left, bold values right, hairline rules between rows
offenders.why: The card already has the right idea (Special Elite quote) but the vitals block is an HTML form. A real intake card is a PRE-PRINTED form — small grotesque print with ruled fill-in lines — completed on a typewriter, values sitting slightly off the printed baseline.

proposals.idea: Kill the overline; label by source
proposals.detail: Delete the tracked-uppercase label pattern globally (all ~151 letter-spacing decls audited to <=0.05em except engraved plaques). Every label picks one of four printed sources: (1) pre-printed form print — Libre Franklin 500 at small size, normal tracking, with ruled boxes and form numbers ('CARD 12-B REV. 3/71'); (2) typed header — Special Elite/Courier Prime with a typed underline of hyphens or ===== ; (3) rubber stamp — heavy caps, see stamp proposal; (4) engraved brass — small caps with inset emboss text-shadow, the ONLY place wide tracking survives.

proposals.idea: Replace Big Shoulders with a wood-type poster pair
proposals.detail: Drop Big Shoulders entirely. Poster voice = 'Ultra' or 'Bevan' (fat-face/Egiziano slab — the fight-bill face) for one-word room names and event bills, plus 'Anton' (an Impact clone; Impact shipped 1965, historically clean) for condensed gothic secondary lines. Use ONLY at poster scale on poster objects; ink texture via 1px blurred text-shadow duplicate + SVG feTurbulence displacement at 0.4 scale so edges bleed like letterpress on cheap stock.

Masthead: bundle 'Chomsky' (free OFL blackletter, NYT-style) or GF 'UnifrakturMaguntia'. Body: 'Noticia Text' (designed for newsprint), justified with hyphens:auto, 2-3 columns via CSS columns. Every story gets a bold condensed gothic headline (Anton, sentence case, tight). Dates/bylines become agate: 7-8pt-equivalent small caps in ink black, never amber. Slight ink-squeeze: font-weight one step heavier than modern taste plus 0.2px blur on body.

proposals.idea: Make the magazine paper with a 70s face
proposals.detail: The Magazine moves to cream stock (reuse --parchment). Display: Cooper Black is THE 1975 magazine face — no faithful GF clone, so bundle a free Cooper-alike or use 'Ultra' with -0.01em tracking as the stand-in slot behind the asset registry. Body: 'Libre Caslon Text' or 'Lora'. Ratings pages become agate tables: rank, name, gym, record in Courier Prime tabular rows with dot leaders (CSS: repeating-linear-gradient dots or ::after '. . . .' overflow-clipped).

Add exactly two handwriting faces: 'Permanent Marker' for marker-on-tape (locker name plates, jar labels, taped-over corrections) and 'Caveat' (or 'Homemade Apple' for a shakier owner) for ballpoint trainer notes — the gym log, 'YOUR READ' on walk-in cards, margin notes on fighter files. Ballpoint blue-black (#2a3550 aged) on paper, chalk off-white on boards. Rotate each note -1.5deg..1deg via nth-child so no two hang identically.

MoodChip/TraitChip/trajectory pills become stamps: Archivo Black caps, stamp-pad red (#a6432a) or bureaucratic blue, rotated -3deg..2deg, eroded by an SVG feTurbulence mask (baseFrequency 0.25, used as alpha) with a faint double-strike offset copy at 60% opacity. 'MUST KEEP / WATCH LIST / CHOPPING BLOCK' is begging to be three stamps on a folder. Same words, larger x-height — scannability improves, the pill dies.

Ban tabular UI sans for game data. Ledger money and fight records: Courier Prime (clean IBM output — Special Elite stays for worn field paperwork). Attribute scores on scouting sheets: typed numerals with ±1px baseline wobble (per-cell translateY) and occasional 85%-opacity strike; recent-form arrows become grease-pencil ticks (Caveat '/' marks), not ▲▼ glyphs. OCR-A (free, bundleable, released 1966) as a garnish on account numbers and license IDs only.

Real typescripts have one weight and no italics: wherever --font-typewriter is used, emphasis becomes underline, ALL CAPS, or x-strikethrough (text-decoration: line-through with 'x' overlay), never synthetic bold/italic (the browser is currently free to fake both). Add ribbon variance: word-level spans at 88-100% opacity via a deterministic hash so re-renders don't shimmer. This one rule makes every typed surface read as a machine, not a font.

hills: No tracked-out uppercase overline labels, anywhere. Wide-tracked caps survive only where metal was engraved (brass plaques, trophy plates). This single habit is 80% of the app's modern accent; if it stays, no font swap will save the fiction.

The Paper and The Magazine are typeset as 1975 print artifacts — blackletter/Caslon masthead, justified hyphenated news body, gothic headlines, black-ink agate, paper stock. They are the game's period anchor; a newspaper in the app's UI voice tells the player the whole world is fake.

One voice per object, mixed by source not hierarchy: a form never borrows the poster face for its heading; typed values never share a font with pre-printed labels; numbers are typed or penciled, never tabular UI sans. If you can't name the machine or hand that made the glyphs, the glyphs are wrong.
fights: Accessibility will object to handwriting (Caveat/Permanent Marker) and eroded stamps for meaningful game state, and to ballpoint-blue on parchment contrast. I'll concede size floors (~16px equivalent) and contrast-checked ink values, but I will not concede the sources themselves — flavor and status text in system-clean type is the whole disease we're treating.

Engineering/performance will object to growing from 4 families to ~8-9 (Ultra/Bevan, Anton, Noticia Text, Libre Caslon, Courier Prime, Caveat, Permanent Marker, bundled Chomsky + OCR-A) plus SVG filter cost on stamps. Subsetted woff2 makes this ~150KB total; I will trade weights and cut Roboto Slab entirely, but a period world cannot be built from four fonts, and I won't preload less than the newspaper needs.

UX/layout will object to rotation, baseline wobble, and stamp erosion on interactive, scannable elements (dev-table statuses, folder tabs, buttons) as noise that slows decisions. My line: imperfection lives on the object at rest — hover/focus states may sharpen and straighten, but I will not ship a straightened, untextured 'interactive mode' that snaps the world back to software.

verdict: This UI is built from exactly one material: dark gradient plastic, tinted warm. Read the CSS and it's the same recipe everywhere — linear-gradient(180deg, dark, darker), 1px border, inset top highlight, rounded corners, amber hover glow. That is the SaaS component recipe wearing sepia. Nothing has tooth, fiber, grain, or manufacturing evidence; the parchment is a flat hex with two soft radial vignettes — beige rectangle cosplaying as paper. Only three SVG components (lockers, portraits, gym background) contain any noise at all, and the locker wear is cloned — eight doors with identical rust ellipses, which reads faker than no rust. A 1975 gym is objects from different makers, different decades, different processes. This UI has one manufacturer: Figma, 2024.

offenders.where: src/components/Button.css (all buttons, every screen)
offenders.tell: One universal rounded-rect gradient plate; hover adds `0 0 16-22px` amber glow
offenders.why: Omnidirectional glow is light emitted by a screen, not reflected off painted steel or brass. A single button construction for every action means every object was made by the same factory — the opposite of a gym assembled over 20 years. Glow is THE tell of digital.

offenders.where: src/screens/GymScreen.css / floor5.png — the five room nav cards
offenders.tell: Five identical floating cards, equal width, equal gap, uniform 1px borders, thin-line amber icons (Feather/Lucide look), hover radial glow
offenders.why: This is the enemy named in the brief: a modern dashboard card row. Outline glyph icons did not exist as physical objects in 1975 — rooms had painted doors, wired-glass windows, screwed-on signs. Nothing here is fastened to anything.

offenders.tell: Fully-rounded outline pill chips with status colors
offenders.why: Colored tag-pills are Linear/Notion vocabulary. A 1975 trainer marks a card with a rubber stamp, a grease-pencil circle, or a typed annotation — never a green-outlined capsule.

offenders.where: src/components/AttributeBar.css (tab_overview.png attribute rows)
offenders.tell: Thin rounded progress-bar track + fill, seven perfectly aligned meters
offenders.why: Progress bars are a fitness-app meter with no 1975 physical analog. The uniform hairline tracks read as data visualization software, not a trainer's assessment of a body.

offenders.where: ArrivalNotice.css / PressRoom.css parchment recipe (frontpage.png, press_paper.png)
offenders.tell: Flat --parchment hex + two radial-gradient vignettes + inset glow; razor-straight edges, uniform radius corners

offenders.where: FighterProfile.tsx Training/Trainer rows (tab_overview.png)
offenders.tell: Native browser <select> dropdowns with OS chrome and chevrons
offenders.why: Browser form widgets are the most literal piece of 2025 software on any screen; they shatter the diegesis instantly. Assignments belong on a clipboard or a pegboard, not in an OS control.

offenders.where: src/assets/lockers.tsx (wall8.png)
offenders.tell: Eight lockers sharing the exact same two rust ellipses, same vents, same handle; grain wash at 7% alpha barely registers; perfect grid
offenders.why: Cloned wear betrays proceduralism worse than cleanliness — real corrosion is where water actually ran. This is the one place noise exists and it's both too faint and photocopied.

offenders.where: FighterProfile tabs + MUST KEEP/WATCH LIST/CHOPPING BLOCK + WALL/LIST toggle (tab_overview.png, devview2.png)
offenders.tell: Equal-width boxed segmented controls with an active fill state
offenders.why: This is an iOS segmented control. The brief hands us the answer: file-folder tab dividers, clipboard clamps, a painted board with a sliding marker — all trivially CSS-able and none of them symmetric boxes.

proposals.idea: One noise, four materials — a baked texture kit in theme.css
proposals.detail: Ship 3-4 static SVG data-URI tiles as custom properties, applied with background-blend-mode — never live filters. --tex-paper: feTurbulence fractalNoise baseFrequency 0.9, 2 octaves, desaturated, ~4% alpha, blend multiply (paper tooth). --tex-plaster: baseFrequency 0.04, 3 octaves, blend overlay at 6% (walls, concrete). --tex-steel: anisotropic baseFrequency='0.008 0.35' for directional brush grain on lockers/plaques. --tex-canvas: repeating-linear-gradient weave (2 crossed 1px repeats at 3% alpha) over noise. Each tile is decoded once and GPU-cached; a surface becomes `background: var(--tex-paper), <aging gradients>, <stock color>`. Every surface in the game gets exactly one of these — flatness becomes impossible by construction.

proposals.idea: Material identity per control class (industrial design spec)
proposals.detail: Buttons stop sharing a factory. Primary/destructive = painted steel plaque: 0px radius, stamped bevel via two hard 1px box-shadows (light top-left, dark bottom-right), --tex-steel, and four corner screwheads as 8px pseudo-element radial-gradients each rotated a few degrees differently (slot direction varies). Secondary = manila shipping tag: --tex-paper, punched reinforced hole (radial-gradient ring), typed label, hangs 1deg off level. Nameplates = brass: vertical brushed linear-gradient (6+ stops), engraved text via text-shadow 0 -1px rgba(0,0,0,.6) / 0 1px rgba(255,240,200,.25), oxidation darkening at edges via inset shadow in green-brown.

proposals.idea: Kill the glow: one lamp, one shadow direction
proposals.detail: Delete every `0 0 Npx` omnidirectional glow. Establish a single global light source (desk lamp, upper-left) and encode it as tokens: --shadow-cast: 3px 5px offsets, --bevel-light top/left, --bevel-dark bottom/right, consistent app-wide. Hover states become physical: paper lifts (translateY(-1px) + shadow grows longer and softer in the lamp direction), steel plaques press IN (inset shadow deepens, translateY(1px)), brass catches light (brighten only the top gradient stop). Interactivity reads through material behavior, not emission.

proposals.idea: A real paper system: three stocks with edges, folds, and stains
proposals.detail: Newsprint (gray-cream, heaviest --tex-paper, visible at 6%), manila (warm, medium tooth), index card (pale, faint ruled lines via repeating-linear-gradient). Each sheet gets: an irregular edge on at least one side (clip-path polygon with 8-12 jittered points — torn; or 0px hard-cut with 0.3deg rotation — guillotined), a fold line (1px linear-gradient dark/light pair across the sheet), corner-anchored aging (radial-gradient tobacco darkening from one corner, seeded per document), and occasional coffee rings (radial-gradient ring, 8-12% alpha, on ~1 in 4 sheets by id hash). The newspaper additionally gets ink-bleed: text-shadow 0 0 0.4px currentColor and slightly imperfect column rules.

proposals.idea: Fasteners: everything on screen is attached to something
proposals.detail: Reusable .tape and .pin primitives. Tape: pseudo-element, rgba(232,222,190,0.45), 2-3deg skew, torn ends via 6-point clip-path polygon, faint darker occlusion shadow under its edges, subtle specular stripe (linear-gradient) because tape is glossy. Pin: 10px radial-gradient sphere (highlight offset toward the lamp) + 2px cast shadow ellipse offset down-right + the paper dimpling slightly (tiny radial darkening under the pinhead). Notices get tape; roster cards get pins in a corkboard (--tex-plaster tinted cork + darker speckle layer); the ArrivalNotice modal becomes a note taped to the glass, not a floating card.

A tiny hash(id) → {rotation -1.4..1.4deg, translate ±2px, wear-variant 0-3} utility drives CSS custom properties per instance. Lockers: rust ellipses positioned from the seed (bottom seam, hinge line, under the handle — where water actually runs), dent count varies, name tapes cut to different lengths at different angles. Lists and grids keep their layout boxes (usability intact) but contents sit off-axis by these amounts. Deterministic, so nothing shimmers on re-render, and it costs one style attribute per element.

proposals.idea: Attribute bars → the trainer's pencil ledger
proposals.detail: Replace AttributeBar with a typed number (typewriter font, baseline jitter ±0.5px via seeded transform) plus a hand-ruled scale: an SVG line run through feDisplacementMap (turbulence scale ~1.5, filter baked into a tiny shared <defs>, static so it renders once) with a grease-pencil fill — a thick stroke with --tex-paper masking its alpha so it looks dry-dragged. Trajectory arrows become pencil check-marks and minus signs. Same information density, same scan speed (number is primary, mark is secondary), zero progress-bar.

proposals.idea: Segmented controls → folder tabs and painted boards
proposals.detail: Profile tabs: file-folder dividers — trapezoid clip-path tops, overlapping via negative margin and z-index, active folder lifted with full --tex-paper and a shadow cast onto the folder behind it, inactive ones darker and tucked. Labels typed on adhesive labels. MUST KEEP/WATCH LIST/CHOPPING BLOCK: one painted wooden board (--tex-plaster over wood-brown, cracked paint via 1px noise-masked lighter layer) with a sliding brass indicator or a chalk circle around the active word. WALL/LIST/DEVELOPMENT: a hook-and-hanging-clipboard metaphor — the active view's clipboard is 'taken down' (foregrounded).

hills: No unmotivated light. Every highlight, bevel, and shadow obeys one lamp with one direction; the omnidirectional glow (`box-shadow: 0 0 N`) is banned from the codebase. If an element brightens, I must be able to say what in the room lit it.

No naked surface. Every element larger than a postage stamp carries a material pass (one of the baked noise tiles + an aging gradient). But texture is always static data-URI tiles — never live feTurbulence filters on elements that animate or scroll. Atmosphere never costs a frame.

No photocopied wear. Two identical instances of the same object are forbidden — imperfection must be seeded per-instance (deterministic hash of id) or omitted entirely. Cloned rust is worse than no rust; it reveals the machine behind the set.
fights: Accessibility will object to noise behind body text, grease-pencil marks, and off-axis rotation as contrast and legibility risks. I'll hold ink-to-paper contrast ratios at readable levels, but I will not sand the tooth off the paper or straighten every sheet — a 4% multiply grain and a 1-degree tilt do not stop anyone reading a roster, and a flat beige rectangle stops everyone believing it.

Engineering/performance will try to cap me at one or two background layers and veto SVG filters wholesale. I'll give up live filters voluntarily (they're in my own hills) but I will fight for 4-6 layered backgrounds and per-instance CSS custom properties on static surfaces — that's composited once and cached; it is not where frames go to die.

Information architecture will defend the five-card floor nav and segmented controls as faster to scan than doors, folder tabs, and painted boards. I say scan speed is a property of hierarchy and lighting, not of rounded rectangles — and the brief explicitly trades the dashboard for a room. If the floor stays a card row, my materials are just wallpaper on a SaaS app and we've failed the whole assignment.

verdict: The lighting is component-emissive, not environmental. The backdrop paints a lamp pool and window shafts, but not one foreground element receives that light — every panel carries its own identical linear-gradient fill, an identical sourceless amber rim (`inset 0 1px 0 rgba(232,181,102,.1)`), a straight-down Material-elevation shadow, and a hover glow. Five nav cards sit in front of five window shafts and none is brighter than another; the newspaper is a uniformly luminous sheet floating in a black void like a phone at night. This is OLED-card lighting wearing amber hex codes. There is no per-room source identity, no shadow direction, no light tokens in theme.css at all — light is hardcoded per component, which is precisely how software glows and rooms don't.

offenders.why: Real objects under a lamp cannot glow or float; light in a room does not react to where you look. This is touchscreen-button feedback, the owner's named enemy.

offenders.tell: A self-luminous document: maximum paper brightness with no gradient across the sheet and no cast shadow from anything.

offenders.why: Steel lockers under fluorescent tubes are lit by the tubes — uniformly-per-bay, with cool spill and specular streaks — not by their own occupancy status. Also nothing in this locker room is fluorescent; it's all desk-lamp amber.

offenders.tell: A pulsing notification LED.
offenders.why: 1975 urgency is a red grease-pencil circle, a note nailed over the sign, or the bare bulb over the message board being ON — never a soft breathing glow, which is pure smartphone.

proposals.idea: One light rig per room, as a scene layer
proposals.detail: Add light tokens to theme.css (--key-x, --key-y, --key-color, --key-reach, --shadow-dx/--shadow-dy) set per room on the root screen element. Render the light as ONE full-viewport pointer-events:none overlay stack ABOVE content: a `mix-blend-mode: soft-light` radial-gradient key pool at (--key-x,--key-y), skewed linear-gradient window shafts in `screen`, and an off-center `multiply` darkness layer replacing .worn. Panels drop their private gradients and become flat material colors — the rig lights backdrop and UI in the same pass, so a plaque standing in a shaft is genuinely brighter than one in shadow.

proposals.idea: Directional shadows from the named source
proposals.detail: Replace every `0 24px 60px` elevation shadow with a two-part directional shadow derived from tokens: a tight umbra (`calc(var(--shadow-dx)) calc(var(--shadow-dy)) 6px -2px rgba(0,0,0,.6)`) plus a longer soft penumbra. Office (lamp lower-right): shadows fall up-left and short. Gym floor (high bulbs): short, nearly under the object. Locker room (tubes): almost shadowless, faint and doubled. One token change re-lights a whole room.

proposals.idea: Kill emissive feedback; hover = catching the light
proposals.detail: Ban `0 0 Npx` outer glows on anything that isn't a fixture. Hover/focus states become optical: a static specular streak (::after, a 20deg near-white linear-gradient sliver at low opacity, angle tied to --key-x) that strengthens on hover, brass label glint via a 1px bright edge, and the shadow shortening slightly as if the object leans toward the lamp. Selection = a clip-on work light or grease-pencil ring drawn in SVG, not brightness(1.12).

Every parchment surface (newspaper, magazine, walk-in card, forms) gets a lamp gradient overlay: `linear-gradient(115deg, rgba(255,238,200,.28) 0%, transparent 45%, rgba(43,30,16,.38) 100%)` in multiply, hot corner matching that room's --key position, plus a soft page-edge shadow onto the desk beneath. Cap base parchment at --parchment-dark; only the lamp hot-spot reaches full #e8dcc0. The Press page should feel read under a lamp at a desk, its far column dimmer than its near one.

Office: one incandescent pool, steep falloff (radial with stops at 0/22/55%), 2700K tint #e8b566, everything outside the pool drops to near-black fast. Locker room: fluorescent tubes — two horizontal cool bands (#c9d4c2 at 8-12% screen blend) with hard cutoffs, one tube flickering via a 4s steps() opacity keyframe on ONE band only (disabled under prefers-reduced-motion). Press: a cold dusty window shaft — gray-blue linear strip with SVG feTurbulence dust masked inside it. Gym floor: hanging bulbs at irregular x-positions, one visibly dead (dark cone), replacing the five perfect shafts.

Game state already carries season and day. Drive two root variables — --daylight-strength and --daylight-color — from date: winter = low raking cold shafts (steeper skew, #b8c4cc), summer = high warm shafts, evening/after-advance-day = shafts at 0 and the lamp pools carrying the whole room. Implement as inline style on the screen root; the overlay gradients consume the variables, so the same CSS re-lights the gym across the calendar for free. Monday morning paper should look like morning.

proposals.idea: Light explains hierarchy — dock UI in the pools
proposals.detail: Stop distributing nav plaques on a symmetric grid and place them where light actually falls: the room signboards hang under the bulbs (each inside its cone, slightly uneven spacing, one half-in-shadow), the gym log clipboard sits at the edge of the lamp pool, the timebar sits in warm floor-bounce (a weak bottom-up amber gradient — wood reflects the lamp). Remove every label and the bright spots alone should still tell you where to look, which is the owner's stated test.

proposals.idea: Delete the app chrome scrims and blur
proposals.detail: Remove all three `backdrop-filter: blur(2px)` (room-door, GymLogBoard, TimeControls) and the video-player top scrim `linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(10,7,5,.94), rgba(10,7,5,.4))` on .gym__chrome/.fp__chrome. The header becomes a painted wall board lit by spill from the nearest window shaft (its brightness varies with --daylight-strength); the cash figure lives on it as a chalk or tag under the same light, not as glowing amber text on a translucent bar.

hills: Nothing emits light except actual fixtures. Zero outer glows, zero pulsing shadows, zero brightness-on-hover on any object that is not a lamp, tube, window, or the moon. If an element needs emphasis, move light onto it or draw attention with a physical mark.

One rig per room, defined once in tokens, lighting background and UI in the same pass. The moment a component ships its own gradient fill and rim light, we are back to cards in a void — I will reject any panel CSS that self-lights.
Every shadow has a direction and that direction agrees with the room's named source. A single straight-down elevation shadow anywhere is a bug, not a style choice.
fights: Accessibility will object to steep lamp falloff and dark corners failing contrast ratios. I will guarantee AA contrast inside the lit content zones — that is what the light is FOR — but I refuse to flatten the room to uniform brightness; a gym at night is dark where nothing happens, and darkness outside the reading area is not a defect.

The art director / asset-replacement pipeline will fight the scene-layer rig: blend-mode overlays above content mean replacement art must be delivered neutral/unlit so the rig can light it, while artists will want to bake lighting into their paintings. Baked light kills time-of-day, per-room re-lighting, and consistency between art and UI — the rig wins.

Engineering/performance will push back on full-viewport mix-blend-mode layers, SVG turbulence dust, and a flicker animation as compositing cost, and the interaction designer will mourn the hover glow as lost affordance. The specular-streak hover is subtler by design — objects in a room don't shout — and two blend layers is a price a game about atmosphere pays.

verdict: This is a competently built modern dark theme wearing a sepia filter. The entire palette is a single hue ramp — background, panels, borders, text, and accent all sit between 25° and 40° of amber-brown — which is exactly how a design system generates "dark mode," and exactly how no physical room has ever been colored. A real 1975 gym is chromatically heterogeneous: green-gray steel lockers, institutional mint plaster, concrete, manila folders, cool newsprint, oxidized brass, sun-faded painted red. None of those hues exist in theme.css. Worse, the accent logic is pure SaaS: amber deployed as a brand color on tabs, links, and progress bars, plus a saturated #7bbf6a success green in alpha-tinted pill chips that could ship in GitHub tomorrow. Color currently says "theme." It must say "material."

offenders.where: src/styles/theme.css (entire token set) — visible on every screen
offenders.tell: Monochromatic value ramp: --ink-black through --amber-bright are one continuous brown gradient; --text-warm (#e8dcc0) is literally the same hex as --parchment
offenders.why: Single-hue dark ramps are the signature of generated design-system palettes. A room built from oak, steel, concrete, paper, and painted plaster cannot share one hue; when text is the same color as paper, nothing reads as a distinct object — it all melts into one sepia screen.

offenders.why: That green does not exist in 1975 pigments — it is the exact colorway of a Linear/GitHub status label. Alpha-tint backgrounds are a compositing trick with no physical analogue; nothing in a gym is 12% translucent green.

proposals.detail: Replace the abstract ramp with tokens named for objects, spanning real hue variety at low chroma: --tobacco #6f5136 (office walls), --oak #7a5c38 / --oak-shadow #4f3a22, --locker-steel #5c635a and --locker-steel-lit #757c70 (green-gray enamel), --gym-green #435243 (painted wainscot/forest green trim), --plaster-mint #98a58e (institutional wall paint), --concrete #8a8578 / --concrete-cold #6d6a62, --brass-oxidized #8a7440 / --brass-polished #c9a55c / --brass-deep #5e4d28, --paint-red-faded #8f4438 (sun-bleached sign red), --charcoal #26241f, --cream-enamel #d8cfb8. Every screen must contain at least two material families so no room reads as one gradient.

proposals.idea: Aging triplets and CSS aging math
proposals.detail: Every material token ships as -fresh/-worn/-old. Codify pigment physics: paper yellows and warms (hue rotates toward 45°, blue channel drops); paint chalks (desaturate 30-50%, lighten toward --concrete); brass oxidizes toward olive (hue toward 70°, value down); reds are fugitive and fade fastest (chroma loss ≫ value loss). Implement with color-mix in oklch, e.g. --paint-red-old: color-mix(in oklch, var(--paint-red-faded), var(--plaster-mint) 35%). This gives artists and CSS the same aging rulebook.

proposals.idea: Kill #7bbf6a — replace semantic green with period inks
proposals.detail: Positive/negative states become marks in real inks: grease-pencil red #8f3b2e (circled = attention), graphite pencil #4a463f (notes, deltas), stamp-pad violet #5c4a63 (official stamps: APPROVED, PLATEAUED), ballpoint blue-black #33404e. If green must exist it is chalk on slate: chalk #dfe0d4 on chalkboard #2f3833, or faded pennant green #6b7d5a as an absolute chroma ceiling. Up/down trajectory arrows become penciled ↗ marks in graphite, never colored UI glyphs.

Reserve the amber ramp exclusively for illumination: lamp pools, window shafts, glints on brass — applied as overlay/multiply layers (radial-gradient rgba(217,154,78,0.08-0.15)) on top of material colors. Selected/active states become physical: active tab = manila folder tab pulled forward (lighter --manila + cast shadow), selected fighter = index card with a red grease-pencil circle. No element may change its own hue toward amber to indicate state.

proposals.idea: Paper stock system — five stocks, five temperatures
proposals.detail: --newsprint #d6d1c2 (coolest, gray-cream, for The Register), --pulp #d4b98a (warm yellowed magazine), --manila #cfae72 (folders, envelopes), --index-card #ece2c8 (fighter cards, faint blue rule lines #9fb0bd), --carbon-flimsy #e8d8b8 with violet carbon text (duplicates, receipts). Each stock pairs with its own ink token and yellowing gradient (edge-in radial multiply of rgba(150,110,50,0.12)). Different documents instantly read as different objects, replacing the universal parchment card.

Give each room an ambient color cast layered over the same material tokens: office/desk = tungsten (multiply overlay rgba(255,178,92,0.07), shadows warm #1a120b); locker room/corridor = fluorescent (overlay rgba(198,214,190,0.06), shadows cooler #141612); press pages = daylight-neutral so newsprint stays cool. Implemented as a per-room --room-light token mixed into surfaces via color-mix. This is how the same steel locker looks different at the desk versus under the tubes — the room lights the interface.

A small library of translucent aging colors applied as ::before/::after layers and SVG feTurbulence fills: --stain-coffee rgba(107,68,35,0.20) (ring ellipses), --nicotine-glaze rgba(180,140,60,0.10) (top-of-panel multiply gradient), --rust-bleed #6e3b23 (radial at screw positions), --tape-shadow rgba(120,100,60,0.25) (masking-tape residue rectangles), --scuff-black rgba(20,16,12,0.30). These are color infrastructure other seats can consume without inventing hexes — ending the current sprawl of 30+ hardcoded hexes outside theme.css.

Bind every type family to an ink, so information provenance is chromatic: typewriter = ribbon blue-black #33383e (slightly uneven via subtle text-shadow); handwritten trainer notes = graphite #4a463f or ballpoint #2f4468; rubber stamps = dried red #8f3b2e or violet #5c4a63 at 85-92% opacity with mask-image noise for partial impressions; poster headlines = --paint-red-faded or --charcoal on paper; newspaper body = soft black #2e2b26, never #000. Ink never reaches pure black or full saturation — ribbons dry out, pads run low.

hills: A chroma ceiling is law: no color on screen may exceed what 1975 pigments plus decades of UV allow — roughly OKLCH chroma 0.11 for any large surface, 0.14 for small ink accents. The #7bbf6a green dies, no exceptions, no 'but it tests well.'
Amber is light, not ink. The accent ramp may only illuminate (overlays, pools, glints); the moment amber becomes a fill color on a control, we are theming a SaaS app again.

Every color token must name a physical material or ink and carry aging variants. I will reject any abstract token (--accent, --success, --primary) in review — if you cannot say what object the color came off of, it does not enter theme.css.
fights: Accessibility: my faded ribbon inks and graphite-on-manila deliberately hover near the 4.5:1 boundary, and violet stamp ink at 88% opacity will fail on some stocks. They will demand brighter text; I will concede size, weight, and letterspacing but not hue brightening — a jet-black typewriter line is a lie about the machine that typed it.

UX/Information design: they will want a consistent green-good/red-bad semantic code so players scan state instantly across screens. I say hue-coded semantics are the most anachronistic pattern in the whole app — state must read through marks (stamps, circles, pencil arrows) in period inks, and I accept that this costs a beat of scanning speed.

Engineering/asset-registry: my per-room light-temperature casts mean no material has one fixed hex — every surface color is color-mix(material, room-light), which complicates the token registry and the drop-in art pipeline. They will push for static hexes per component; I will not accept a steel locker that is the same color under a desk lamp and a fluorescent tube.

verdict: This is a handsome 2025 dark-mode app lit with amber — a Spotify skin for a speakeasy, not a gym. The writing is period-literate (the fictional papers get real 1975 days-of-week right; the walk-in card and ledger tab are genuine artifacts), but almost nothing on screen would survive the test "could Cus D'Amato's office contain this?" Progress bars, status pills, segmented controls, native dropdowns, HUD cash tickers, red iOS badges, backdrop-filter blur, and — worst of all — PRINT rendered as gold text on black. In 1975 the press was black ink on cheap paper under a light; The Ring analog here looks like a crypto dashboard. The bones (rooms, paper metaphors, warm palette) are right; the material layer is entirely missing.

No widget the owner couldn't buy, type, paint, or staple in 1975: zero pills, badges, progress bars, segmented controls, native dropdowns, or blur. Every control must name its physical ancestor before it ships.

Every string of text declares its source. Typewriter means someone typed it; pencil means someone wrote it; poster type means someone printed it. If two unrelated objects share a face, one of them is lying.
fights: Accessibility will object to newsprint agate, faded mimeograph purple, and pencil-gray ledger entries as low-contrast. I will not brighten ink that was never bright; the correct fix is size, spacing, and lighting (the desk-lamp hotspot), not #FFFFFF text on 'aged' paper.

Engineering/performance will resist per-surface SVG feTurbulence grain and halftone patterns as filter-cost bloat and push for flat tinted gradients. Flat tint is exactly the 'vintage-colored modern app' the owner is firing us over — texture is the deliverable, so we budget for it (rasterize filters to data-URI tiles if needed, but they exist).

Game/UX design will defend numeric bars, chips, and the HUD cash ticker as 'decisions stay fast.' I'll hold that a grease-pencil mark on a printed scale carries identical information at identical speed, and that a 1975 trainer made faster decisions off an index card than any of us do off a dashboard.

verdict: This is a modern dark-mode dashboard wearing sepia, and its deepest failure is shared by both halves of my seat: it commits to permanent night, then prints almost everything in 8-11px letterspaced microtype on near-black. Tertiary text (#6f6450 on #14100c) sits around 3.3:1, "EMPTY" lockers and dimmed stale stats are near-invisible by design, form trends hang on 8px green/red arrows, and mood is a 9px colored dot. Psychologically the floor is a void — no walls, no midground, no human traces — which reads abandoned, not lived-in: the exact stress signature the brief forbids. The saving grace is that 1975 and accessibility agree: paper under a lamp is a high-contrast object. Keep the existing focus-visible ring and reduced-motion handling; everything else about the reading surface must flip.
