proposals.detail: Invert the contrast architecture: the room stays dark, but all decision-critical data moves onto lit paper objects — parchment (#e8dcc0) with ink (#2a2118) is ~12:1, versus today's muted-on-black at 3-6:1. Dev table becomes a typed roster sheet, attributes a scout's evaluation form, the profile a manila folder's contents. The desk lamp 'lighting the page' (a soft radial gradient peaking at full paper luminance over the content zone) makes high contrast diegetic instead of fighting the mood.

Codify environment plane vs document plane. Environment (walls, lockers, desk) takes unlimited grime; the document plane obeys a wear budget: SVG feTurbulence grain at opacity <=0.06 over text, coffee rings/tape residue confined to margins and corners, text-block rotation clamped to +/-2deg, no stain may cross a line of type. Implement as CSS custom properties (--wear-grain, --wear-tilt) so art direction turns wear up without ever touching the text zone.

Kill every pill. Statuses become rubber stamps: word set in a condensed grot (Oswald works), inside a rough rectangular or oval border, in one of exactly two period ink colors (red #a6432a, blue-black #2a3548), roughened via an SVG feTurbulence+feDisplacementMap filter, minimum 13px x-height, always angled <=4deg. Meaning is carried by the word and the border shape (oval = temperament, box = trajectory), never by hue — CVD-safe and 1975-true. The green #7bbf6a is deleted from the codebase.

Must Keep / Watch List / Chopping Block become three physical trays or clipboard clips on the desk; the fighter's index card visibly sits in one, with a stamped label on the tray. Status is then encoded three redundant ways — spatial position, container label, stamp — satisfying color-independence while making the highest-stakes decision in the game feel like moving a man's card toward the door. aria-labels carry the same words for screen readers.

Replace 8px colored arrows with hand-drawn pencil annotations at >=14px: a short drawn arrow plus the word ('up', 'flat', 'fading') in a handwriting face, graphite gray #4a3e2e on paper (>=7:1). Staleness stops being opacity and becomes diegetic notation: fresh reads in pen, old reads as pencil with a written date ('as of Mar') — different material, same full contrast. Direction is carried by drawn shape + word, never hue.

Add --type-floor-data: 14px and --type-floor-label: 12px to theme.css and purge the fifty-plus 8-11px declarations. Letterspaced all-caps permitted only >=12px and only for genuinely environmental text (a sign, a stamp); anything the player must read to decide gets >=14px. Period authenticity survives — 1975 government forms used 10pt Pica typewriter, which at arm's length subtends more than 14px on screen. Small type was never part of the fantasy; small UI text is a 2015 habit.

The gym floor needs walls: painted concrete wainscot (two-stop gradient + noise), rubber mat flooring, a corkboard, chain-link, radiator — CSS gradients and SVG filters, all registry-slotted for future art. Environmental psychology: prospect-refuge — visible boundaries and midground objects are what make a space feel safe and inhabited; a black void with spotlights is the classic 'liminal space' stress image. Raising ambient midground luminance also lifts every contrast ratio for free.

Focus/hover = the lamp pulls to the object: a warm radial brighten that raises the focused element to full contrast, layered ON TOP of the retained 2px :focus-visible outline (restyled as a brass glint, never removed). Notifications slide in as paper (<=300ms, single axis) instead of modal pop; the .worn vignette gets a hard rule — pointer-events:none it already has, but it must also never overlap an interactive text zone at more than 0.15 alpha. Fluorescent flicker, if added, stays under 3 flashes/second and behind prefers-reduced-motion, which the codebase already honors globally — preserve that block verbatim.

hills: The 4.5:1 floor is diegetic law: any text a player needs to make a decision meets 4.5:1 (7:1 below 16px), and no wear effect — grain, stain, dimming, vignette — may drop it below that. 'Faded ink' is a look, not an opacity value on live data; if information must read as faded, fade the container, not the contrast of the words.

Color never carries meaning alone. Every status/trend/mood is redundantly encoded by a word, a drawn shape, or a physical position (which tray, which board, which drawer). The green/red arrow-and-dot system dies, and no hue outside the material palette ever encodes state.

Imperfection may never be motion or flicker: no permanent ambient animation on the content plane, no fluorescent strobe above 3Hz ever, all environmental movement behind prefers-reduced-motion, and keyboard focus-visible survives every restyle — a brass glint is fine, but the outline stays.
fights: Art direction / set dressing: they will want coffee rings across the roster, pencil notes at 30% opacity, and text on crumpled tape at an angle — I will hold the wear budget (stains in margins only, +/-2deg tilt, 4.5:1 pencil) and they will call the result 'too clean to be 1975.' I'd rather be slightly clean than unreadable; a cared-for gym IS cleaner where hands touch it daily.

Lighting/cinematography: the current identity is a dark room with amber pools, and my core move — flipping dense data onto bright lit paper — will read to them as 'blowing out the mood.' I will not accept muted-cream-on-leather as the default reading surface for tables; the lamp lighting the page is the compromise, and the page gets full luminance.

Typography: the type specialist will argue authentic 1975 sources are small — agate box scores, elite typewriter, 6pt form footnotes — and that my 14px data floor and 12px caps floor flatten period texture. I concede small type for pure set dressing (margins of the newspaper, poster fine print) but every number the player acts on meets the floor, even if the 'real' 1975 document would have been smaller.

Asset architecture / art direction: I need per-gym procedural brand variation — rival letterheads, sign styles, business-card snips seeded per gym id. They will want one placeholder per component type. I will not accept a world where every gym's paper comes off the same printer.

UX: I want CASH out of the persistent chrome and into the office (cashbox, ledger page, a bill clip on the desk). UX will insist money must be visible at all times for decisions. A floating KPI is the single loudest dashboard tell in the game; put a small bill-clip object in the office doorframe if they need a glance.

Accessibility: gold-leaf arc lettering on dark glass, worn stencils, and oxblood rubber stamps will get flagged for contrast. I will accept larger sizes and careful value tuning, but I will not accept flattening the sign into high-contrast sans-serif text — a legible-but-flat sign is not a sign.
hills: The gym name must exist as a painted or stamped MARK, never as a typeset UI string. If the name renders in the app's display font inside a flex header, there is no brand — there is a label.

Paper provenance: every document the gym issues carries the gym's letterhead; every document received carries someone else's. The player should be able to tell whose paper they're holding with the text removed.

One house color, chosen at founding, used sparingly. A 1975 neighborhood gym owned one bucket of trim paint — locker trim, door stencil, stamp ink. A coordinated palette is corporate; one stubborn color is a brand.

proposals.detail: Replace .gym__chrome's name string with an SVG hand-painted window sign: gym name arched on an SVG textPath in gold-leaf fill (linear-gradient gold with a darker keyline via paint-order: stroke), city + 'BOXING · TRAINING' on a straight rule beneath, all sitting on dark glass with a faint interior reflection (radial-gradient) and chipped letters (feTurbulence-driven mask eating small bites from strokes). The Walk-In Card banner becomes 'FIGHTER REGISTRATION — [GYM NAME]' on this letterhead with a rubber-stamped RECEIVED date.

An SVG notary-style stamp: gym name curved around the roundel border, monogram center, date across the middle; oxblood ink, rotated −2 to −4deg, uneven ink coverage via an feTurbulence alpha mask so no two impressions render identically (seed from document id). Use it as the universal 'this gym acted' mark: SIGNED on new fighters, CUT on releases, PAID in the ledger. Replaces pill badges and toast confirmations with a physical act.

Locker door trim stripes pick up the same house color. The '0/2 FOCUSED SLOTS' stat becomes a chalk tally on a small board hung on that wall.

Each competitor gym renders as a collected artifact, not a card: seeded per gym id, rotate 4–5 period identities — engraved business card (serif, centered, hairline border), fight-poster snip (woodtype, two-color), athletic-club crest letterhead, cheap mimeo flyer (typewriter, purple-ink tint). Pinned at slightly different angles on a corkboard in the office. Player instantly reads tier from paper quality — an 'ESTABLISHED' pill becomes embossed card stock versus a mimeographed flyer.

Kill 'YOUR GYM · LOCKER ROOM' trails. Each room screen gets its physical sign as the title object: OFFICE on a frosted-glass door pane (black hand-lettering, viewed straight on), LOCKER ROOM as the wall stencil, PRESS as a wire news rack label. The player's monogram roundel sits small and constant in one corner of every gym-owned screen — the brand as a maker's mark, replacing the generic breadcrumb prefix.

Rework StepGymName: as the player types, the window-sign SVG renders live above the input — letters appearing as painted strokes (stroke-dashoffset transition). '⟳ Surprise me' becomes 'Ask the sign painter,' which flips a paper sketch (rotate + new name). Follow with the paint-chip pick for the house color and the stamp being pressed onto the founding papers. Same three inputs as today; the brand is born as objects instead of strings.

verdict: This gym has no brand — it has a workspace label. "Hell's Kitchen Boxing" exists exactly once as a 22px string in a translucent app bar, beside a cash KPI, above breadcrumbs that literally replace the name with "YOUR GYM." There is no mark, no sign, no letterhead, no stamp, no house color, no EST. date — while rival gyms in the database get founding years the player's own gym lacks. The gym's paperwork (walk-in cards, notices) is anonymous UI stationery, and competitors render as identical templated cards, so the fight town has no visual politics. Real 1975 gyms were obsessive self-branders on a budget: gold-leaf windows, stenciled walls, one bucket of trim paint, a rubber stamp on everything. Strip the labels today and nothing tells you whose building this is — the owner's own test fails at the front door.

The motion system is disciplined, tokenized, and reduced-motion safe — good engineering, wrong vocabulary. There is exactly one gesture in the whole game: a polite ease-out fade-rise (--ease-warm, 140/280/600ms) applied identically to steel lockers, paper cards, whole rooms, badges, and tooltips. Rooms materialize with an opacity+scale(1.015) cross-fade like an iOS modal; the walk-in card — the game's heartbeat — enters like a Figma dialog and, when you decide a man's fate, leaves with no motion at all; lockers bolted to a wall levitate 3px on hover; news arrives as a glowing toast and a pulsing badge. Nothing has mass, nothing lands, nothing swings, slams, or settles. Everything moves like light; in this gym, only light should move like light.

offenders.why: The single most 2020s-app pattern in the codebase. In 1975 nobody's gym emits floating status pills; a message is a note someone left, and notes are put somewhere, not faded in.

offenders.where: src/screens/GymScreen.css:150-160 — .room-door:hover translateY(-4px) + amber glow box-shadow + slide-in 'enter' microcopy
offenders.tell: Marketing-site card hover: lift, glow, hover-revealed CTA sliding in from the left
offenders.why: Painted signboards standing in a dark gym levitate and emit light when pointed at — pure Stripe/Linear. A physical sign should respond like a thing being touched or lit, not like a hoverable card.

offenders.where: src/screens/WalkInViewer.css:16-36 + WalkInViewer.tsx — wiv-fade scrim + wiv-rise 12px fade-up; card swaps within a sequence have zero motion

offenders.why: A glowing, breathing red pill is an artifact of phones. The 1975 equivalent of 'something is waiting' is a card wedged in a door, an envelope on the desk, a light left on in the office — not a throbbing counter.

offenders.where: src/components/Locker/LockerWall.css:23-27 — .locker:hover translateY(-3px) + filter brightness
offenders.tell: Hover-lift on grid items
offenders.why: Steel lockers are the heaviest objects in the room and they float upward when pointed at. Inverts the entire material logic: the immovable thing moves the most weightlessly.

offenders.where: src/rooms/LockerRoom.css:50 — transition: width var(--t-med) on the locker capacity meter
offenders.tell: Smoothly animating progress-bar fill
offenders.why: An eased width tween is dashboard KPI language. Physical tallies change in steps — a peg moved, a chalk mark added — they click to the next state; they do not interpolate.

proposals.detail: Replace --ease-warm with a small physics vocabulary in theme.css: --ease-paper (cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1), 180–260ms, always paired with 0.5–2deg rotation — paper never travels straight); --ease-steel (cubic-bezier(.55,0,.35,1), 320–450ms, hard stop — a clunk, no soft tail); --ease-stamp (cubic-bezier(.7,0,1,.5), 90–120ms accelerating IN — impacts speed up, they never ease out); --ease-swing (damped keyframes for hinged/pinned things); plus steps(2..4) for anything electrical. Rule: fades/opacity tweens are reserved for LIGHT only (lamps, windows); objects move, light fades.

proposals.idea: Deal the walk-in card, file the verdict
proposals.detail: WalkInCard enters as a card laid on a desk: keyframe from translate(30px,-40px) rotate(4deg) scale(1.05) with a large soft drop-shadow, landing at rotate(-0.8deg) scale(1) shadow tight — 240ms --ease-paper. Each decision gets an exit before unmount (a 350ms 'deciding' state in WalkInViewer.tsx): 'locker' slides the card right and down onto an implied stack; 'turn away' slides it left off the desk edge with shadow growing then gone; 'later' tucks it toward the bottom (the office drawer). The next card deals in overlapping the exit by ~100ms. Kill wiv-rise; keep the scrim but make it the desk lamp dimming the floor (brightness filter), not a gray overlay.

MUST KEEP / WATCH LIST / CHOPPING BLOCK, locker assignment, and cut-from-gym resolve with a stamp: the label appears scale(1.6)→1 in ~110ms --ease-stamp, opacity snapping to 1 at the moment of contact, resting at a per-instance ±1.5deg rotation (seeded from fighter id), ink edge roughened with an SVG feTurbulence displacement mask; the paper beneath does one 60ms 1px translate jitter on impact. This is the sound of a thunk rendered in motion.

Replace room-enter/room-rise with a hallway move: outgoing view translateX(-5%) + brightness(0.6), incoming from translateX(6%) with light coming up, 380ms --ease-steel — you turned your head and walked. For the Office specifically, a door-swing variant: incoming content transform-origin at the left edge, rotateY(-6deg)→0 with slight perspective, as the door opens onto the desk. Back-to-the-floor reverses direction. All transform/filter only, fully CSS, snap-to-end under prefers-reduced-motion.

Ban translateY lifts. Lockers: on hover the handle/latch pseudo-element jiggles (rotate keyframe 0→3→-2→0, 260ms, origin at the latch) and the door cracks 2deg on rotateY with hinge-side transform-origin, a 2px sliver of interior light appearing at the gap. Room signboards: the bulb above snaps on with steps(3) flicker (opacity 0→1→0.4→1 over 180ms) — incandescent, not eased glow. Paper rows/cards: a corner-curl pseudo-element (small gradient triangle) grows 3px, or the sheet shifts 1px rotate(0.3deg) as if a fingertip pinned it.

proposals.idea: Pinned things swing on the pin
proposals.detail: Gym log entries, notices, and corkboard items animate around their pin: transform-origin at the pin position, damped wobble keyframes rotate 3deg→-1.8→0.8→-0.4→final (~500ms), settling at a per-item crooked angle (±1.5deg via nth-child or seeded custom property). Replace ArrivalNotice's centered fade-drop with a note tacked to the doorframe: it enters with this pin-swing at the door's edge, not centered like a system banner. Replace door-badge-pulse with a static wedged card sticking out of the door jamb — presence, not pulsing, is the signal.

proposals.idea: Time passes as light and a calendar flip
proposals.detail: Advance Day/Week: the desk calendar's date card does a two-frame rotateX flip (top-hinged, steps(2), ~200ms — flip cards don't interpolate), while the whole floor container dips brightness(0.55) and returns over 400ms, like the room's day turning over. New log lines and newspaper items appear only after the light returns — the world changed while you blinked. Pure filter + transform; reduced-motion users get an instant date change with a single subtle brightness step.

FighterProfile tabs: the active file-divider physically rises 3px and overlaps its neighbors via z-index (dividers already overlap 4px, offset from perfect alignment); incoming page content enters translateY(6px) rotate(0.3deg)→0 with --ease-paper 200ms — a sheet pulled to the top of the pile; the outgoing page does NOT animate (it's simply behind now — folders don't fade). Same treatment for WALL/LIST/DEVELOPMENT toggles in the locker room.

hills: Every animated element declares a material — paper, steel, brass, rubber, or light — and uses that material's easing and duration. Opacity tweens are reserved for light sources only. A generic fade on an object is a bug, not a default.

No hover levitation, ever. translateY lift + glow shadow is banned across the codebase. Hover must read as touch or light: a latch jiggle, a door crack, a corner curl, a bulb flicker. If the heaviest object in the room moves the most easily, the whole set collapses.

Consequence motion is non-negotiable: every player decision (stamp, sign, assign, cut, turn away) produces a visible physical result within ~400ms — the card slides to a stack, the stamp lands, the drawer shuts. State must never 'just update'; a React re-render is not an event in a room.
fights: Accessibility will object to my stamp-impact jitter (1px paper shake), accelerating ease-in impacts, and damped pin-wobble as vestibular risk and to 350ms decision-exit animations as slowing expert players. I'll honor prefers-reduced-motion with instant snap states, but I will not soften impact frames for everyone — a stamp that eases out is not a stamp.

Visual/lighting design will defend the smooth amber hover glow and pulsing badge as 'desk lamp warmth.' I say incandescent light snaps and flickers via steps(); it does not interpolate. We will fight over the room-door hover and every glowing box-shadow loop.

Engineering will resist replacing the single --ease-warm token with a per-material set, and will especially resist exit-before-unmount choreography in WalkInViewer (React state must hold a 'deciding' phase for ~350ms). They'll call it complexity; I call it the difference between a gym and a component library.
